item.title: Pony Toolchain in 2026: ponyc vs Corral vs Stallion — Is Capability-Secure Actor Programming Worth It?
item.description: Your actor system passed 4,000 unit tests, survived a staging soak, and still deadlocked eight minutes into Black Friday. That is the dirty secret of message-passing concurrency: the compiler never told you that two actors could touch the same mutable state, because in most languages it cannot tell you. Pony was built to close that hole — every reference in Pony carries a reference capability (iso, val, ref, box, trn, tag) and the compiler rejects any program where a data race is structurally possible. No locks, no synchronized, no runtime race detector needed: races become type errors.
